text:
Maya R: hey team — unexpected: flight delayed and I need to run to the gate. Can someone take primary for ~2.5h starting now? I'm currently primary until 21:00 UTC. :airplane:

Sam O: i can cover the first hour while you get out the door. after that i'll need backup, can Trinh take the rest?

Trinh P: i can take over from ~2041234800 (in ~12m) until 21:00 UTC. will be shadowing on home laptop. 

Maya R: thanks @Sam O and @Trinh P — much appreciated. leaving quick notes: no active P1s, but eu-west tokenization job showed spikes earlier (see #incidents thread). key runbook pointers below.

Maya R: runbook excerpt:
```
If API error rate > 3% for 5m AND tail latency p95 > 1s:
 1) check model pool health: `redwoodctl pools list --region eu-west`
 2) if pool below 50% capacity, promote warm nodes or failover region: `redwoodctl pools scale --name ml-eu-1 --count +2`
 3) open incident, tag with `impact:production` and page secondary if primary unresponsive
```

Sam O: noted. where is that runbook saved? link pls.

Maya R: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/ONCALL-Runbook-Serving — bookmarked the exact section 'latency spikes + routing'

oncall-bot: Auto-check: current open incidents: 0. Active alerts: eu-west latency spike (warning). Next scheduled maintenance: none.

Trinh P: quick question — if eu-west degrades, do we fail traffic to us-central by default? last time we had routing fallback but want to confirm thresholds.

Maya R: routing policy: failover when 10%+ requests hit errors OR when p95 exceeds 2s for >10m. fallback to us-central is controlled by policy `failover-eu-on-latency` (see console > routing > policies).

Sam O: ok. i'll keep an eye on the alert channel and run the prefix-cache check if latency persists.

Maya R: also: if you need to hand off mid-shift, we use ops-rotation tool: 
```
/ops-rotation assign primary @Trinh P until 2041236000 --note "temp swap, maya flight"
```

Sam O: running that now -> `/ops-rotation assign primary @Trinh P until 2041236000 --note "temp swap, maya flight"`

ops-rotation: Rotation update queued. Confirm to apply: `confirm 1` or cancel.

Trinh P: confirm 1 (confirming takeover at ~2041234800). :thumbsup:

ops-rotation: Rotation applied. Primary: Trinh P (2041234800 -> 2041236000). Secondary: Sam O. Change logged (ticket OR-7521).

Maya R: perfect, thanks. tagging runbook lines I rely on: `/runbook show latency-spike` is handy.

Sam O: a few quick local checks i'll run while you head out:
- curl health endpoints to verify kv-cache: `curl -sS http://svc-cache-eu/health | jq .`
- tail serving logs for evictions: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serving --since=5m`
- check billing/burst policies in console if we need to spin up warm nodes

Trinh P: i'll keep phone on. if we see >5% error rate escalate to P1 and page oncall-pagers. Escalation note: page both primary+secondary if P1 after 2 minutes w/ no ack.

Maya R: one last note — client X has scheduled batch at 22:00 UTC; if we get sustained latency we may need to throttle them. contact SRE on-call for batch-throttle permission.

Sam O: ack. i'll mute non-critical alerts and keep the important ones loud.

Maya R: leaving now. thanks again — will check in after landing. :airplane:

Trinh P: got it, taking over. everyone ping me in thread if anything pops.

oncall-bot: Reminder: please update your status if you are covering someone else's primary shift: `/status set oncall-covering Trinh P (temp)`

Sam O: status set.

Trinh P: quick verification — i can see the scheduled takeover in the console and the rotation note OR-7521. all good.

Maya R: thanks team, appreciate the quick cover.

Sam O: safe travels! :wave:

Trinh P: all clear for now. will escalate if anything changes.
